gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ the flames with buckets for an hour by the time the firemen arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour by the time … arrived' — past perfect continuous for duration before a past moment.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our cousins in Melbourne next month — the flights are booked.
gaps.hint: a booked arrangement for next month
gaps.explanation: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: are visiting.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: They ___ married in a small ceremony in 2011.
gaps.explanation: A dated single event takes the past simple: got.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.
